title: PlunderSpell core loops: what the hits teach

short.lead: Viral co-op games spread through chaos, but they keep players through progress. How to Fish sold 10 million copies by doing both, then lost 78% of its players in a month because its ladder was only three islands long. PlunderSpell has the chaos and an approved end goal. What it lacks is the middle: coins buy nothing yet, so there is no hour-to-hour climb.
short.hint: Tap a finding to see the evidence and what it means for PlunderSpell.
items: Chaos-first games (Lethal Company, R.E.P.O., Content Warning, PEAK) have four friends, a dangerous place, physics and proximity voice, and the best clips. Progress-first games (How to Fish, Schedule I, Cookie Clicker, Scritchy Scratchy, Balatro) have a number that keeps rising, purchases that change how you play, and a far goal. The biggest recent hit, How to Fish, is both.

items.alt: Bar chart of copies sold: Phasmophobia 22 million, R.E.P.O. 16.4, Lethal Company 15, PEAK 10, How to Fish 10, Schedule I 9, Buckshot Roulette 8, Vampire Survivors 7.9, Content Warning 5.2, Balatro 5, Gamble With Your Friends 2, Scritchy Scratchy 0.75.

items: Every hit loses most of its players

Each game's latest month as a share of its best: Lethal Company 2%, R.E.P.O. 16%, PEAK 29%, How to Fish 22% after one month. Every bump after launch came within a month of new content; a fix-only patch did not bring How to Fish players back. A viral launch is a spike, not a base, and the base is kept by something new to reach for.

items.alt: Line chart of monthly average players as a share of each game's best month, by months since launch. All four games fall steeply; Lethal Company ends at 2%, R.E.P.O. 16%, PEAK 29%, How to Fish 22% after one month.
items.caption: Steam monthly average players, from SteamCharts and Steambase, read 2026-10-25.

items: Rewards on three clocks at once

The progress games reward you every few seconds (a catch, a scratch), every few minutes (a purchase that changes what you can do) and every few hours (a new island, region or reset), with a far goal above it all. PlunderSpell has the seconds clock (grab, cast, haggle), half of the minutes clock (raid and sell), no hours clock, and its end goal is planned but not built.

items.alt: Grid comparing seven games across seconds, minutes, hours and end goal. PlunderSpell today is strong on seconds, partial on minutes, missing hours, and its end goal is only planned.
items.caption: Solid: strong. Dim: partial. Dashed: missing. My judgement from the research files.

items: What makes incremental progress feel good

Six things recur. Every purchase opens something new, not a 5% bonus. The systems feed each other with no dead ends (fish pay for guns, guns open islands, islands pay more). Random spikes ride on a steady climb (golden cookies, rare fish, jackpots, R.E.P.O.'s monster orbs). A near goal and a far goal are always visible. And there is a 'next' after the end, such as Cookie Clicker's ascension or Balatro's harder stakes.

No ending (Lethal Company). A ladder that runs out (How to Fish's three islands). Power that makes the game easier instead of the player better (Vampire Survivors; Game Maker's Toolkit asks: 'Did you get better, or did the game just get easier?'). Automation that kills the hands-on part (Scritchy Scratchy's top critical review). Friends' schedules (How to Fish readers). A gambling look that cost Balatro a PEGI 18 rating and YouTube age gates.

The Wick, as the model for every true form: it sees only by its own fire, turns one way, and kills with one catch. Haggling with Plus, Satis and Vale. Coins as heavy pouches. The Ophan's demand every 3 to 5 raids and the goal of beating it. Spells earned from Porta upward. Death never wipes the Lair.
Four questions that shape the proposal
Stage 3, the proposal, is built on your answers to the four Choices below: what follows the Ophan, what coin buys, how long the climb is, and whether there is gambling.
Pick an answer for each choice, then send the reply.

changes: new
Coin buys things
The Market sells, not only buys.

Today a haggle pays out coin and the coin has nowhere to go (no buy code exists on any branch read). Every progress game in the research turns its currency into new abilities within minutes. This is the first gap to close.
Coins pay only the Collector's debt, which the fear pass removes.
Spells, tools, Lair rooms and luck to buy at the stalls.
Every haul leads to a purchase you can feel in the next raid.
new
A visible ladder to the Ophan
Rungs you can see, in the Lair.

How to Fish always shows the next island and the way home. PlunderSpell's far goal exists only in a design document. A ladder in the Lair, such as rungs on the ledger or a growing orrery, shows how close the company is.
The goal is approved and invisible.
A ladder of named rungs toward beating the Ophan.
You always know what the next step is.
new
Random spikes
Luck on top of the steady climb.

Golden cookies, rare fish variants, jackpots and R.E.P.O.'s monster orbs are what players clip. Candidates for PlunderSpell: rare gilded variants of loot, a vendor's lucky night, a relic that pays big if it survives the trip home.
Loot worth is a roll per piece and nothing more.
Rare, visible spikes of luck.
Moments worth shouting about.
new
A 'next' after the end
Beating the Ophan starts something, not nothing.
Lethal Company has no end; How to Fish ends and players leave. Cookie Clicker and Balatro end a run and offer a harder, richer one. Choice 'After the Ophan' below decides this.
No plan for after the end goal.
A new cycle, or a clean ending.
The game has a reason to come back to.
chg
Unlocks are new verbs
Most upgrades change what you can do.
Power that makes the castle easier
Options and knowledge that make you better
Keeps the fear the owner approved: the castle stays deadly while the company grows. The quota and the Ophan grow with you, and each guard's counter is knowledge you learn.
keep
Raids stay hands-on
Automate chores, never the raid.
Scritchy Scratchy's critics say the game dies once robots scratch for you. Carrying, casting and escaping stay in the players' hands.
keep
Nobody starts over
Already decided in the fear pass.
Content Warning and Lethal Company wipe progress on one failure. PlunderSpell keeps the Lair and learned spells on death, which is the right call for a long climb.
choices: After the Ophan is beaten, what happens?
A new cycle, harder and richer
Like Cookie Clicker's ascension: keep some progress, face a stronger hunter.
Credits roll; a new save starts over.
Option A gives a reason to keep playing, the gap that cost How to Fish its players.
New things to do, plus a few small stat upgrades
Spells, tools, Lair rooms and routes.
Option A keeps the castle frightening while the company grows.
How long should a regular group take to beat the Ophan?
Long enough to climb, short enough to finish.
Option A is my estimate, not a measured figure: longer than How to Fish, whose players left once it was done, and short enough for a friend group to finish.
Wagers woven into the loop, in-game coin only
Dice with vendors, double or nothing on a haul, cursed relics.
Keep luck in the loot alone.
Option A gives random spikes without a casino look, which is what cost Balatro its rating.

wrapup.summary: An analysis of twelve indie hits, showing that PlunderSpell lacks the hour-to-hour progress ladder between its raids and its end goal.
wrapup.changing: Nothing is built. Stage 3 turns this into a proposal page with the loops, the enemy roster, the timeline and four workstreams.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the four choices.
wrapup.next: Once you send your answers, I write the stage 3 proposal.
